% Both xr's old release, which \usepackage{xr}[=v5] loads, and xr-hyper,
% then hyperref. xr-hyper's \externaldocument is the one used. The page
% builds, and each reference prints as with xr-hyper alone: from an .aux
% that LaTeX wrote under hyperref, whose \externaldocument gives the URL of
% its PDF, its number, page, name, and \autoref as in the PDF, with no
% link and no URL; from an .aux that tex4ht wrote under hyperref, with its
% .xref, a link to that document's page.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xr}[=v5]
\usepackage{xr-hyper}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}[https://example.org/ext.pdf]
\externaldocument[H-]{test-xrboth/old}
\begin{document}
CaseH \ref{X-ss}, page \pageref{X-front}, named \nameref{X-thm},
auto \autoref{X-thm}.

CaseI \ref{H-oss}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.
\end{document}
